comment: Mutation testing for the DOCUMENTATION PIPELINE. A SECOND config rather than entries in stryker-config.json because Stryker mutates one 'project' per run. This library exists as a non-test project precisely so it can be mutated: Stryker treats test projects as the test-projects, so a renderer living in DwarfMapper.Generator.Tests could never be a mutation target, and nothing would prove the doc tests catch a defect in the renderer itself. Run via scripts/housekeeping.ps1 -Mutation (needs: dotnet tool install -g dotnet-stryker --version 4.16.0). RE-MEASURED 2026-08-19 on Stryker 4.16.0 after the T3-H1 write-back guard, against the WHOLE test suite (4,787 tests discovered), 12 logical cores: score 67.96 % (193 detected of 284 scoreable — 191 killed + 2 timeout; 54 survived, 37 uncovered, 75 compile errors excluded), 5 min 27 s wall-clock. break is that score floored to 67. THE PREVIOUS 83.10 % (236/284, same day, pre-guard) WAS INFLATED BY THE T3-H1 DEFECT ITSELF: with write-back live, the first destructive mutant emptied the committed documents on the REAL tree, and every later mutant session then compared its renderer output against that polluted committed text — 43 mutants were 'killed' by the destruction, not by any assertion about their own behaviour. All 43 are no-ops on the current documentation corpus and survive on a stable tree: real corpus holes, exposed (not created) by the guard, catalogued under 'T3-H1 fix' in Issues/ledgers/T3-mutation-survivors.md. The mutant space is IDENTICAL across the two runs (284 scoreable both times; the only flips are those 43 plus one Timeout that became a clean Kill), so 67 is the leg's first HONEST floor, not a regression. Historical: before 2026-08-16 the config could not run at all ('comment' sat inside 'stryker-config', which Stryker 4.16 rejects) and its 'mutate' globs were repo-root-relative, producing a VACUOUS run that still exits 0; the inherited break of 70 had never been measured. NOTE 1 — THERE IS DELIBERATELY NO 'additional-timeout' HERE, AND THAT IS A MEASURED DECISION, NOT AN OVERSIGHT. Its sibling stryker-config.json needed one because two of its timeouts were clock artifacts on mutants that cannot hang. Both timeouts in this leg GENUINELY HANG, so they are real detections and the default ceiling is correct: SnippetScanner.cs L138 and L139 delete the 'kept.RemoveAt(...)' inside 'while (kept.Count > 0 && string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(...))' — each an unconditional infinite loop with a covering set of 1 test, not the whole-suite geometry that manufactures a spurious timeout. (The pre-guard run had a third: DocSnippetInjector.cs L39 deleting the 'i++' inside 'while (i < lines.Length)' — on the stable post-guard tree it is Killed outright before the loop is reached, a Timeout-to-Killed flip, still detected either way.) Adding a 120 s cushion would only make genuine hangs cost extra minutes. IF a Timeout ever appears here on a mutant that provably cannot hang (no loop, no unbounded recursion, no blocking call), raise 'additional-timeout' — never filter the test set. NOTE 2 — WHY THIS LEG IS FAST AND ITS SIBLING IS NOT: ZERO of its 284 scoreable mutants are 'static', so Stryker attributes per-test coverage to every one of them and the covering sets are tiny (1,603 test executions in total). The generator leg has 85 static mutants, each of which re-runs the entire suite, and it costs 21 minutes. The difference is coverage attribution, not test quality. NOTE 3 — THIS LEG USED TO REWRITE TRACKED DOCUMENTATION, AND THE MECHANISM IS GUARDED SINCE 2026-08-19 (T3-H1). The doc-generation tests heal-or-fail into README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/diagnostics.md, docs/options.md and samples/DwarfMapper.Gallery/README.md, and the mutants under test are the code that writes them; the first completed run left three of those files EMPTIED (2,523 deleted lines across five files, reverted). The verified mechanism: Stryker 4.16 has NO sandbox for test execution — it swaps the mutated assembly into each test project's REAL bin folder in place (leaving 'X.dll.stryker-unchanged' beside it), so AppContext.BaseDirectory is the real bin, every repo-root walk resolves the real repository, and a mutated renderer wrote its output over the real files. The guard is RepoWriteGuard (tests/DwarfMapper.Generator.Tests/Contracts — deliberately in the TEST project, because a guard inside this mutation target could itself be mutated off): every test-side repo write routes through it, and it REFUSES the write when it detects a mutation run ('*.stryker-unchanged' beside the test assembly, or a 'StrykerOutput'/'.stryker-tmp' ancestor). NO TEST IS EXCLUDED from this leg and every staleness assertion still runs and still fails — only the write-back is suppressed — so the kills are unchanged; a post-run 'git status' is expected CLEAN, and RepoWriteGuardTests pins both the detection and the refusal. The pre-guard MutantControl pollution history is in Issues/ledgers/E3-E1-report.md, the fix measurement in Issues/ledgers/T3-mutation-survivors.md under 'T3-H1 fix'. NOTE 4 — the 'mutate' globs must be PROJECT-relative ('**/Name.cs'), never repo-root-relative: Stryker resolves them against src/DwarfMapper.DocTooling, so a repo-root path matches nothing, every mutant is dropped with 'Removed by mutate filter', and Stryker STILL EXITS 0. Assert-MutantsWereTested (scripts/housekeeping.ps1) exists for exactly that hazard; it counts scoreable statuses in the JSON report and returns 284 for this run. NOTE 5 — Stryker mutates and COMPILES the whole project regardless of these globs (568 mutants created; 183 dropped by the mutate filter; 75 rolled back as compile errors; 26 dropped by the block-already-covered filter; 247 tested plus 37 uncovered), and only then filters what is TESTED. The report therefore contains every file in the project; the five named here are the only ones carrying scoreable statuses, and that is the non-vacuity check to make. NOTE 6 — there is deliberately NO 'test-projects' key. It would be INERT: Stryker discovers the solution and enumerates EVERY test project in it, so such a list does not select the test set; see NOTE 3 in stryker-config.runtime.json for the measurement that established this. It was removed rather than corrected, so nothing here pretends to scope anything. NOTE 7 — THE MARGIN TO break IS THREE MUTANTS. 193/284 is 67.96 %; 190/284 is 66.90 % and FAILS. break is the floored measured score, as in all three configs — and note the second way the score can move: the two Timeouts COUNT AS DETECTED, and they are genuine hangs, so any environment that stops hanging on them (a test-level timeout wrapper, a different scheduler) drops the score with no test having changed. If a run lands under 67, check the Timeout bucket BEFORE assuming a regression. NOTE 8 — the original 11 survivors and 37 uncovered mutants are catalogued, with a real-hole-or-equivalent judgement for each, in Issues/ledgers/T3-mutation-survivors.md; the 43 additional survivors the T3-H1 guard exposed (pollution kills reclassified as the corpus holes they always were) are recorded there under 'T3-H1 fix'. Raise break only by killing survivors. NOTE 9 — 'low' MUST STAY >= 'break' or Stryker 4.16 REFUSES TO RUN AT ALL ('Threshold low must be more than or equal to threshold break') — and refuses with EXIT CODE 0, so nothing downstream notices except Assert-MutantsWereTested. T3 raised break from 70 to 83 but left low at 80, which made this leg unrunnable from 2026-08-19 until the T3-H1 fix re-ran it; low now tracks break (a report-colouring threshold, not a ratchet). Whenever break moves, move low with it.
